citation.title: Length Scale Control in Topology Optimization using Fourier Enhanced Neural Networks

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On four benchmark problems, Fourier-TOuNN produced lower compliance values than SIMP while adding approximate minimum and maximum length-scale control.
claim.key_phrase: lower (better) than both SIMP and TOuNN
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: The article reports no head-to-head wall-clock speed-up factor. Fourier-TOuNN example runtimes are 4–6 seconds, described as consistent with mesh-based methods.
claim.alternatives: Section 5.1 reports 4–6 seconds for Figure 9 examples and describes this as consistent with mesh-based implementations; it does not claim a speed advantage over SIMP.

baseline.solver: Finite-element analysis; solver type not stated
baseline.hardware_classical: Intel i7-6700 CPU at 2.6 GHz, 16 GB RAM (Section 5)
baseline.hardware_ml: Intel i7-6700 CPU at 2.6 GHz, 16 GB RAM (Section 5)
baseline.training_time: Per-problem optimization; 150 minimum and 500 maximum iterations (Section 5)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; no offline training dataset used
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance and target volume fraction (Section 5.1, Figure 9)
baseline.quality_gap: Figure 9 reports lower compliance for Fourier-TOuNN than SIMP across four benchmarks; exact pairs appear in Figure 9.

R1.evidence: Section 5.1, Figure 9: primary comparison is compliance quality; the paper does not claim a speed advantage over SIMP.

R2.evidence: Section 5 states both approaches ran on the same CPU; no R2 efficiency criterion is established.

R3.evidence: Section 5 describes per-problem optimization with no offline training or data-generation stage.

R4.evidence: Section 5.1 reports compliance and volume targets; Section 5.5 notes disconnected topologies for a setting, but no failure or infeasibility rate is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four benchmark problems in Figure 9, followed by additional single- and multi-material design experiments (Sections 5.1–5.6).

notes: The article gives total times for Figure 9 examples but not separate SIMP times, so no speed-up can be derived. The article states that Python code is available online; its license is not specified in the paper.
